scope: Experimental SIM-6 two-domain frictionless or Coulomb-penalty node-to-surface contact with small or finite sliding, finite-deformation kinematics for finite sliding, linear penalty normal behavior, optional bounded planar/curved initial adjustment, and bounded quasi-static increments.

lanes.acceptance: The v2 contract admits only the declared two-domain small/finite-sliding frictionless or Coulomb-penalty envelope and rejects missing capability profiles, mixed contact/sliding behavior, mismatched finite-deformation assumptions, invalid coefficient/stick slope/increment bounds, stale identity, and geometry outside the declared search/adjustment bounds.

The CalculiX adapter emits deterministic face-based secondary/primary surfaces, explicit SMALL SLIDING for small kinematics or default finite sliding plus NLGEOM, optional request-bounded ADJUST, linear pressure-overclosure, explicit coefficient/stick-slope *FRICTION when requested, bounded *STATIC increments, and final CDIS/CSTR output.

evidence.smallSlidingContactCard: *CONTACT PAIR, TYPE=NODE TO SURFACE, SMALL SLIDING

lanes.acceptance: Bounded FRD and STA parsers reject invalid magnitudes and incomplete increment histories; request-aware normalization bounds CalculiX's small tensile regularizer, rejects nodal shear outside the declared Coulomb coefficient, preserves signed COPEN, recovers omitted-node clearance against the final deformed triangulated primary surface, and retains interface ownership, pressure/gap/slip/shear datasets, resultant force, and final step time.

A real Gmsh/CalculiX planar patch fixture demonstrates the expected approximately uniform pressure plus global and contact-force equilibrium. Refinement and penalty trends remain isolated in their own required lane.
Independent real solves demonstrate active closing under compressive loading and complete opening under prescribed tensile separation without tensile contact traction.

Real planar fixtures with +0.05 mm clearance and -0.05 mm interference are admitted inside an explicit 0.06 mm adjustment bound, converge under displacement-controlled compression, transmit compressive contact force, retain final penetration below the bound, and emit the mandatory mesh-adjustment warning.

A deformable half-cylinder on a planar foundation demonstrates a center-high, edge-decaying Hertz-type pressure strip, contracting peak-pressure changes under refinement, fine-mesh contact width agreement, exact secondary-body force equilibrium, and reduced bounded penetration under a stiffer penalty.

evidence.fixture: R10 x 10 mm half-cylinder on planar steel foundation

lanes.acceptance: A deliberate one-increment ceiling and immediate cancellation fail closed, terminate descendants, clean native files, quarantine fields/results, and cannot be resurrected by a late process exit.

Paired real displacement-controlled frictionless/frictional solves recover negligible frictionless tangential force, nonzero Coulomb-limited shear and slip, normalized shear/slip datasets, and tangential equilibrium between contact and drive reactions.

A real displacement-controlled block moves 4 mm tangentially across a 2.5 mm mesh while finite sliding and NLGEOM update contact projection; contact remains active, slip follows the prescribed travel, and the frictionless tangential resultant stays negligible.

A real R10 x 10 mm half-cylinder begins 0.05 mm above a planar foundation; closest-triangle mesh admission permits only nodes within the explicit 0.06 mm capture bound, CalculiX adjustment activates the patch, and the solve retains force equilibrium and bounded penetration.

evidence.fixture: R10 x 10 mm half-cylinder on planar steel foundation

lanes.acceptance: An independent qualified engineer approves the formulation, fixtures, tolerances, sign conventions, assumptions, and exact reviewed commit.
